name: Parikshit
summary: Parikshit is the grandson of Arjuna and the Kuru king who inherits the throne after the great war. He is remembered for listening to the Bhagavata Purana in his last days.
about: Parikshit appears in the Mahabharata as the son of Abhimanyu and Uttara and the grandson of Arjuna. The texts say Krishna saved him in the womb from Ashvatthama's weapon. He becomes the king at Hastinapura after the Pandavas leave. Many Puranas say he confronted Kali, the spirit of the present age, and kept him confined to a few places. After a rash act toward the sage Shamika, his son Shringi cursed him, and the king spent his final week hearing the Bhagavata Purana from Shuka. Historians also place a king of this name in the Kuru state of about 1200 to 900 BCE, mentioned in the Atharvaveda and later Vedic texts.
kidSummary: Parikshit was the grandson of the hero Arjuna and a wise king. The stories say that when he was a baby, Krishna protected him. As king, he sent away Kali, the spirit of the present age of quarrels, who is not the goddess Kali. In his last week he listened to a sage named Shuka tell stories about Krishna.

story.title: A baby is protected
story.text: After the great war, Arjuna's grandson is born. In the texts, Krishna saved him from a danger, and the baby is named Parikshit.

story.title: The cow and the bull
story.text: Years later, King Parikshit finds a bull standing on one leg and a sad cow. In the Bhagavata, they stand for dharma and the earth, and Kali, the spirit of the age of quarrels, is harming them. This Kali is not the goddess Kali.

story.title: Kali is limited
story.text: The king spares Kali but allows him only a few places, such as gambling and drink, where wrong ways are likely to grow.

story.title: A hasty act
story.text: The king treats a quiet sage rudely. The sage's son sends a curse that the king will die within seven days.

story.title: Seven days of stories
story.text: Parikshit spends his last days hearing about Krishna from the sage Shuka. Many call his calm during these days an example of facing the end with peace.

teaches: Spend precious time on what matters

facts.text: The Bhagavata Purana explains Parikshit as 'the examiner': having seen a divine figure in the womb, he would test every person to find it again. The Mahabharata gives 'the tested one'.
In the Bhagavata Purana, the unborn Parikshit saw a thumb-sized figure with a club guard him in the womb, and this vision shaped his search for the divine for life.
In the Bhagavata account, Uttara was terrified by the blazing weapon, so her mother-in-law Subhadra prayed to her own brother Krishna, who shielded the child in the womb.
The Atharvaveda praises a Kuru king Parikshit as 'raja vishvajanina', roughly 'king of all people', whose land overflowed with milk and honey and happy people.

Scholars place Parikshit in the Middle Vedic period: Witzel dates his dynasty to about 1200 to 1100 BCE, Raychaudhuri argued for the 9th century BCE. Witzel credits his Kuru circle with first collecting the Rig Veda, Sama Veda and Khilani.
According to the Mahabharata, Parikshit married Madravati, a princess of Madra, and ruled for sixty years.
The Shatapatha Brahmana (13.5.4) gives Parikshit four sons: Janamejaya, Bhimasena, Ugrasena and Shrutasena. It says all four performed the horse sacrifice.
The Atharvaveda hymn praising Parikshit includes a little home scene: a Kuru householder prepares grain while his wife keeps asking what drink to fetch, and the ripe barley bends over the path.
Vedic literature knows only one Parikshit, but later texts seem to describe two. Raychaudhuri thought the second might come from later genealogy-making or bardic duplication.
Tradition regards Parikshit as a reincarnation of Satya Yuga, the personified first age, which makes his meeting with Kali, the personified age of strife, a striking match-up.
After his coronation Parikshit performed three sacrifices and travelled across the land while doing so, and it was on one of these journeys that he met Kali.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Parikshit finds Kali, disguised as a man, beating a cow and a bull. The bull is Dharma, standing on one leg, and the cow is the grieving earth.
The Bhagavata says Parikshit spared Kali but restricted him to five places: gambling, taverns, houses of immoral conduct, slaughterhouses and gold.
In another telling of the tale, Kali slips into Parikshit's golden crown, which once belonged to Jarasandha, and clouds his mind. The king later says that gold is where Kali lives.
The sage Shamika, saddened by his son's curse, sent his disciple Gaurmukha to tell Parikshit everything. The king heard the news and accepted his fate.
Parikshit placed a dead snake around the neck of a meditating sage named Shamika. Shamika's son Shringi cursed him to die of a snakebite within seven days.
One account traces Takshaka's grudge to the burning of the Khandava forest: after Arjuna set fire to the Naga realm, Takshaka vowed to avenge himself on one line of the Pandavas.
The Parikshit article calls Takshaka the Naga ruler of Taxila, and the one through whom Shringi's curse was carried out.
In the Mahabharata's Astika Parva, the Naga king Takshaka reached Parikshit disguised as a worm hidden in a fruit, after he had turned the healer Kashyapa back by offering him more wealth.
In one retelling of the snake sacrifice, the priests chanted offerings to Indra along with Takshaka, so Indra too began to be drawn toward the fire, until Astika stopped the sacrifice.
Shuka's name is linked to the parrot. The Skanda Purana says it comes from his habit of repeating everything he heard, and a cave tied to him is called Shukachari.
Naga Panchami falls on the fifth day of the bright half of Shravana and recalls the day Astika stopped the sacrifice. People pour milk on anthills and avoid digging the earth that day.

quiz.q: Parikshit was the grandson of which hero?
quiz.why: His father Abhimanyu was Arjuna's son.

quiz.q: Whom did Parikshit meet disguised as a man hurting a cow and a bull?
quiz.why: The Bhagavata says it was Kali, with Dharma as the bull.

quiz.q: Who told the Bhagavata Purana to Parikshit?
quiz.why: Shuka, a son of Vyasa, narrated it.

quiz.q: Which festival recalls the end of his son's snake sacrifice?
quiz.why: Astika's intervention is remembered on Naga Panchami.

quiz.q: What does the name Parikshit mean in the Bhagavata Purana?
quiz.why: He was to examine everyone to find the figure he saw in the womb.
